name: Adam
occupation: Caretaker of the Garden of Eden
family_members: Sons: Cain, Abel, Seth (and other unnamed sons/daughters)
associated_events: Creation
The Fall (eating the forbidden fruit)
Expulsion from Eden
short_description: The first human being, formed by God from the dust and placed in the Garden of Eden; his disobedience with Eve brought sin into the world.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Created without sin, but his disobedience in the Garden is the biblical account of humanity’s Fall.

name: Eve
family_members: Sons: Cain, Abel, Seth (and other unnamed sons/daughters)
associated_events: Creation
The Fall (eating the forbidden fruit)
Expulsion from Eden
short_description: The first woman, formed by God from Adam's rib to be his companion; deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and shared it with Adam.

name: Noah
roles: The one righteous man of his generation
associated_events: The Great Flood
Building the Ark
The Rainbow Covenant
short_description: Warned by God of a coming flood, Noah built an ark and preserved his family and the animals, becoming the ancestor of all people after the flood.

notes.before_or_after_flood: His life spans the event itself — born before the flood, he lived roughly 350 more years after it (Genesis 9:28).

name: Abraham
family_members: Sons: Ishmael, Isaac (and sons by Keturah)
associated_events: God’s covenant call
Journey from Ur to Canaan
Binding of Isaac on Mount Moriah
Covenant of circumcision
short_description: Called by God to leave his homeland for Canaan, Abraham became father of the Israelite nation through a covenant promise; Scripture calls him a model of faith despite notable moral lapses.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Praised as the father of faith (Romans 4), but twice deceived others by claiming Sarah was only his sister (Genesis 12, 20).

name: Moses
associated_events: The Exodus from Egypt
Parting of the Red Sea
Receiving the Ten Commandments at Sinai
40 years in the wilderness
short_description: Raised in Pharaoh's household, Moses led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt and received the Law at Mount Sinai, though he himself was barred from entering the Promised Land.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditionally credited as author of the first five books of the Bible (the Torah/Pentateuch).
notes.good_bad_neutral: A model of faith and leadership, but struck the rock in anger against God’s instruction (Numbers 20) and was barred from Canaan as a result.

name: David
associated_events: Defeating Goliath
Anointed king by Samuel
Adultery with Bathsheba and the death of Uriah
Establishing Jerusalem as capital
short_description: A shepherd who killed the giant Goliath and became Israel's greatest king, David wrote many Psalms; his reign was marred by adultery with Bathsheba and the killing of her husband Uriah.

notes.prophet: Not usually titled a prophet, but Peter describes him speaking prophetically about the Messiah in Acts 2:29-31.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditionally credited with about half the Psalms (73 carry a Davidic superscription); the book as a whole has multiple authors.

name: Solomon
associated_events: Building the First Temple
Judgment of the two mothers
Visit of the Queen of Sheba
Turning to idolatry in old age
short_description: David's son and successor, renowned for God-given wisdom and for building the First Temple in Jerusalem, though his many foreign wives later led him into idolatry.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Tradition credits him with Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs; scholars debate how much of each he personally wrote versus later compilers.

name: Daniel
associated_events: The fiery furnace (his three friends)
The lions' den
Interpreting Nebuchadnezzar's dreams
Writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast
short_description: A Judean noble taken captive to Babylon, Daniel rose to prominence interpreting dreams and stayed faithful to God, famously surviving a night in a den of lions.

name: Samson
associated_events: Superhuman strength as a Nazirite
Riddle at his wedding feast
Betrayal by Delilah (his hair cut)
Pulling down the temple of Dagon
short_description: A judge of Israel granted supernatural strength through his Nazirite vow, Samson's downfall came through his relationship with Delilah, though he died destroying a Philistine temple.

name: Jonah
approximate_period: Traditional 8th century BC (reign of Jeroboam II)
associated_events: Fleeing to Tarshish
Swallowed by a great fish
Preaching to Nineveh
Nineveh's repentance
short_description: A reluctant prophet who fled God's call to preach to Nineveh, was swallowed by a great fish, and later resented God's mercy when the city repented.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditionally credited as the book’s author, though it is written in the third person.

name: Jesus
family_members: Brothers named in Scripture: James, Joseph, Judas, Simon
associated_events: Virgin birth
Baptism by John the Baptist
Sermon on the Mount
Crucifixion
Resurrection
short_description: The central figure of the New Testament, believed by Christians to be the Son of God and promised Messiah; crucified under Pontius Pilate and, per Christian teaching, raised from the dead.

notes.king: Titled "King of the Jews" (John 19:19) and described as reigning in a messianic sense (Revelation 19:16), but he did not rule an earthly kingdom the way David or Solomon did.
notes.priest: Hebrews calls him a great high priest "in the order of Melchizedek" (Hebrews 5-7) rather than a Levitical priest by ancestry.
notes.good_bad_neutral: The New Testament consistently presents Jesus as sinless (Hebrews 4:15; 2 Corinthians 5:21).

name: Peter
associated_events: Called as a fisherman to follow Jesus
Walking on water
Denying Jesus three times
Pentecost sermon
Vision of clean and unclean animals
short_description: A fisherman called to be one of Jesus's twelve apostles, Peter became a leader of the early church despite once denying knowing Jesus three times before the crucifixion.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: 1 Peter is broadly attributed to him; the authorship of 2 Peter is more debated among scholars.
notes.violent_death: Church tradition (not the Bible itself) holds that Peter was crucified in Rome; John 21:18-19 is read as a prophecy of this.

name: Paul
family_members: A sister is mentioned, unnamed, with a nephew (Acts 23:16)
associated_events: Persecuting Christians before his conversion
Conversion on the road to Damascus
Missionary journeys
Shipwreck en route to Rome
Imprisonment in Rome
short_description: Once a zealous persecutor of the early church, Paul was dramatically converted on the road to Damascus and became the New Testament's most prolific missionary and letter-writer.

notes.apostle: Not one of the original Twelve, but claims apostleship through his direct encounter with the risen Christ (1 Corinthians 15:8-9; Galatians 1:1).
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditionally credited with 13 New Testament epistles; the authorship of the Pastoral Letters (1-2 Timothy, Titus) is debated among modern scholars. He is not considered the author of Hebrews.
notes.good_bad_neutral: Before his conversion he persecuted and consented to the killing of Christians (Acts 8:1, 9:1-2); afterward he became a chief architect of the early church’s mission.
notes.violent_death: Church tradition holds he was beheaded in Rome under Nero, but this is not recorded in the Bible itself.

name: Bartholomew
associated_people: Philip (often paired with him in apostle lists)
associated_events: Called as one of the Twelve
Present at the Ascension
short_description: One of Jesus's twelve apostles, always listed among the Twelve but given no individual narrative in the Gospels; many traditionally identify him with Nathanael in John's Gospel, though the text never states this directly.

notes.name: Widely identified with "Nathanael" from John 1:45-51, but that link is inference, not a stated fact — the Synoptics and Acts only ever call him Bartholomew.

name: Nathan
associated_events: Confronting David over Bathsheba and Uriah with the parable of the ewe lamb
Announcing God's covenant promise to David
Securing Solomon's succession to the throne
short_description: A court prophet during King David's reign, Nathan delivered God's covenant promise to David and famously confronted him over his sin with Bathsheba using the parable of the poor man's ewe lamb.

notes.name: Distinct from the "Nathan" listed among David's own sons in 2 Samuel 5:14 — this Nathan is the prophet.

name: Deborah
associated_events: Judging Israel under the palm tree
Commissioning Barak to fight Sisera
Victory over the Canaanite general Sisera
The Song of Deborah
short_description: A judge and prophetess who led Israel, Deborah commissioned Barak to defeat the Canaanite army and celebrated the victory in the Song of Deborah.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Judges 5 ("The Song of Deborah") is presented as composed jointly by Deborah and Barak.

name: Gideon
associated_events: The sign of the fleece
Reducing his army to 300 men
Defeating the Midianites with trumpets and jars
Making a golden ephod that became a snare
short_description: Called by an angel while threshing wheat in hiding, Gideon led Israel to victory over the Midianites with just 300 men, though he later made a golden ephod that led Israel into idolatry.

notes.king: Israel offered to make Gideon king after his victory, but he refused, saying "the LORD will rule over you" (Judges 8:22-23).

name: Joshua
associated_events: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan
Succeeding Moses as leader
Crossing the Jordan River
The fall of Jericho
Dividing the Promised Land among the tribes
short_description: Moses's faithful assistant and one of the twelve spies, Joshua succeeded Moses to lead Israel across the Jordan River and conquer the Promised Land.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Tradition credits him with most of the Book of Joshua, though it records his own death (Joshua 24:29-30), implying a later hand completed it.

name: Caleb
associated_events: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan
Giving a faithful minority report with Joshua
Receiving Hebron as his inheritance at age 85
short_description: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan, Caleb and Joshua were the only two who urged Israel to trust God and take the land; he received Hebron as his inheritance at age 85.

name: Ruth
associated_events: Leaving Moab to stay with Naomi ("Where you go I will go")
Gleaning in Boaz's fields
Marrying Boaz as kinsman-redeemer
short_description: A Moabite widow who loyally stayed with her mother-in-law Naomi, Ruth married Boaz and became a great-grandmother of King David, later listed in the genealogy of Jesus.

name: Esther
associated_events: Becoming queen of Persia
Fasting before approaching the king uninvited
Exposing Haman's plot to destroy the Jews
Establishment of the Feast of Purim
short_description: A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, Esther became queen of Persia and risked her life to expose a plot to exterminate her people, leading to the origin of Purim.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: The book itself is anonymous, though Esther 9:29 records Esther writing "with full authority" to help establish the Purim observance.

name: Nehemiah
approximate_period: Traditional 5th century BC (reign of Artaxerxes I)
associated_events: Serving as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes
Rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem in 52 days
Opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah
Public reading of the Law with Ezra
short_description: A Jewish cupbearer to the Persian king, Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem and led the rebuilding of the city's walls in the face of fierce opposition.

name: Nicodemus
associated_events: Visiting Jesus by night (John 3)
Defending Jesus before the Sanhedrin
Bringing spices to prepare Jesus's body for burial
short_description: A Pharisee and member of the Jewish ruling council who visited Jesus at night to ask about being 'born again,' later helping prepare Jesus's body for burial.

notes.disciple: Never explicitly labeled a "disciple" in the text, but his defense of Jesus and role in his burial are widely read as signs of secret faith (John 19:38-39).

name: Barnabas
associated_events: Selling his field and giving the proceeds to the church
Vouching for Paul to the Jerusalem apostles
First missionary journey with Paul
Sharp disagreement with Paul over John Mark
short_description: A Levite from Cyprus whose name means "son of encouragement," Barnabas vouched for the newly converted Paul and became his missionary companion on the first missionary journey.

notes.apostle: Called an apostle alongside Paul in Acts 14:14, though he was not one of the original Twelve.

name: Timothy
associated_events: Joining Paul's missionary team at Lystra
Being circumcised by Paul out of sensitivity to Jewish sensibilities
Receiving two personal letters from Paul
short_description: A young church leader raised in the faith by his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois, Timothy became one of the apostle Paul's closest companions and the recipient of two New Testament letters.

name: Elijah
roles: Prophet to the northern kingdom of Israel
associated_events: Announcing a drought to Ahab
Contest with the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
Fed by ravens at the Kerith Ravine
Fleeing Jezebel to Mount Horeb
Taken up to heaven in a whirlwind
short_description: A fiery prophet who confronted King Ahab and defeated the prophets of Baal in a dramatic contest on Mount Carmel, Elijah was taken up to heaven alive in a whirlwind.

notes.violent_death: Elijah never died — he was taken up to heaven alive in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11).

name: Elisha
associated_events: Receiving Elijah's mantle and a double portion of his spirit
Healing Naaman the Syrian of leprosy
Restoring the Shunammite woman's son to life
Multiplying a widow's oil
short_description: Elijah's chosen successor, Elisha performed numerous miracles including healing Naaman's leprosy and raising a boy from the dead, though one account describes him cursing a group of youths who mocked him.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Performed many acts of mercy and healing, but 2 Kings 2:23-24 records him cursing a group of youths who mocked him, after which bears mauled them — a passage often discussed as morally complex.

name: Jehu
associated_events: Anointed king by a prophet sent by Elisha
Killing King Joram of Israel
Having Jezebel thrown from a window
Destroying the worshippers of Baal
short_description: Anointed king of Israel to destroy the house of Ahab, Jehu violently purged Baal worship from Israel, though Scripture later critiques the excessive brutality of his methods.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Carried out God's judgment on Ahab's dynasty, but Hosea 1:4 condemns "the blood of Jezreel" that Jehu shed, and he later tolerated the golden calves at Bethel and Dan (2 Kings 10:29).

name: Hezekiah
associated_events: Removing idols and reforming worship
Miraculous defeat of Sennacherib's Assyrian army
Extending his life 15 years after illness (the sundial sign)
Showing his treasures to Babylonian envoys
short_description: One of Judah's most faithful kings, Hezekiah led major religious reforms and saw Jerusalem miraculously delivered from an Assyrian siege, though he later prideful showed off his treasures to Babylonian envoys.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Scripture calls him one of Judah's best kings (2 Kings 18:5), but Isaiah rebukes his prideful display of the royal treasury to Babylonian envoys, foretelling future exile (Isaiah 39).

name: Josiah
associated_events: Becoming king at age eight
Rediscovery of the Book of the Law during Temple repairs
Sweeping religious reforms and a Passover celebration
Killed in battle against Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo
short_description: Becoming king at age eight, Josiah led Judah's last great religious reform after the Book of the Law was rediscovered in the Temple; he was killed in battle against Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo.

name: Jeremiah
roles: Prophet to Judah during its final years
associated_events: Called as a prophet in his youth
Warning of Jerusalem's coming destruction
Imprisoned and thrown into a cistern
Witnessing the fall of Jerusalem
Forced into exile in Egypt
short_description: Known as the "weeping prophet," Jeremiah warned Judah of coming judgment for decades, was persecuted for his message, and witnessed the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon.

notes.priest: Jeremiah 1:1 identifies him as one of "the priests that were in Anathoth," though his primary role in Scripture is as a prophet.
notes.married: God explicitly commanded Jeremiah not to marry or have children as a sign to Judah (Jeremiah 16:1-4).
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Author of Jeremiah; Lamentations is traditionally (though not explicitly in the text) attributed to him as well.

name: Hannah
family_members: Son: Samuel (and later three more sons, two daughters)
associated_events: Praying fervently for a son at Shiloh
Vowing to dedicate her son to the LORD
Giving birth to Samuel
Her song of praise after dedicating Samuel
short_description: A barren woman who prayed fervently for a child, Hannah dedicated her son Samuel to the LORD's service at the tabernacle after God answered her prayer.

notes.prophet: Not explicitly titled a prophetess, but her prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1-10 is widely read as prophetic and is echoed in Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55).

name: Eli
associated_events: Mistaking Hannah's silent prayer for drunkenness
Raising the boy Samuel at the tabernacle
His sons' corruption as priests
Falling backward and dying upon hearing the ark was captured
short_description: High priest and judge at Shiloh who raised the boy Samuel, Eli failed to restrain the wickedness of his own sons, and died upon hearing that the Ark of the Covenant had been captured.

notes.good_bad_neutral: A faithful priest in many respects, but judged by God for failing to restrain his sons' corruption (1 Samuel 2:27-36, 3:11-14).

name: Abigail
approximate_period: Traditional 11th-10th century BC (before David became king)
roles: Wife of Nabal, later wife of David
family_members: Son by David: Chileab (also called Daniel)
associated_events: Interceding with David to prevent bloodshed against her husband Nabal's household
Nabal's death after Abigail's intervention
Becoming one of David's wives
short_description: Described as wise and beautiful, Abigail intervened to stop David from taking violent revenge on her foolish husband Nabal, and became David's wife after Nabal's death.

name: Boaz
associated_events: Allowing Ruth to glean in his fields
Redeeming Ruth and Naomi's family land as kinsman-redeemer
Marrying Ruth
short_description: A wealthy landowner in Bethlehem, Boaz showed kindness to Ruth and acted as kinsman-redeemer to marry her, becoming an ancestor of both David and Jesus.

notes.family_members: Matthew 1:5 names his mother as Rahab, likely the same Rahab who hid Israel's spies in Jericho (Joshua 2), though this identification isn't stated within the Book of Ruth itself.

name: Zacchaeus
associated_events: Climbing a sycamore tree to see Jesus
Jesus inviting himself to stay at his house
Pledging to repay everyone he had cheated fourfold
short_description: A short, wealthy chief tax collector in Jericho, Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus and, after Jesus visited his home, pledged to repay everyone he had cheated four times over.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Introduced as a wealthy tax collector (a profession associated with extortion in that era); his encounter with Jesus leads to public repentance and restitution (Luke 19:8).

name: Martha
associated_events: Hosting Jesus and being distracted with much serving while Mary sat at his feet
Her brother Lazarus's death and resurrection
Confessing Jesus as the Messiah before Lazarus was raised
short_description: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, Martha welcomed Jesus into her home and, though once gently rebuked for anxious busyness, later made a powerful declaration of faith that Jesus was the Messiah.

notes.disciple: A close friend and host of Jesus who made a strong confession of faith (John 11:27), though not one described as traveling with him like the Twelve.

name: Lazarus
roles: Friend of Jesus raised from the dead
associated_events: Dying of illness in Bethany
Being raised from the dead by Jesus after four days in the tomb
Reclining at a dinner honoring Jesus afterward
short_description: A close friend of Jesus from Bethany, Lazarus died and was raised from the dead by Jesus four days later, one of the Gospels' most famous miracles.

notes.disciple: Scripture calls him someone Jesus loved (John 11:3, 36) but does not explicitly label him a "disciple."

name: Mary Magdalene
associated_people: The other women at the tomb
associated_events: Delivered by Jesus from seven demons
Following and supporting Jesus's ministry
Present at the crucifixion
First to see the risen Jesus and announce the resurrection to the disciples
short_description: A woman delivered by Jesus from seven demons, Mary Magdalene became one of his most devoted followers and was the first person to see him and announce his resurrection.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Popular tradition sometimes conflates her with the unnamed "sinful woman" of Luke 7 or with Mary of Bethany, but the Gospels never identify her as either.

name: Obadiah
approximate_period: Debated; commonly placed shortly after the fall of Jerusalem, 586 BC
associated_people: The nation of Edom (addressed in his prophecy)
associated_events: Pronouncing judgment on Edom for its violence against Judah
short_description: Author of the shortest book in the Old Testament, Obadiah pronounced God's judgment on Edom for gloating over and profiting from Jerusalem's downfall.

notes.approximate_period: The exact date of Obadiah's ministry is debated among scholars; the book is commonly placed shortly after Jerusalem's fall to Babylon in 586 BC because it responds to Edom's actions during that catastrophe.

name: Nahum
approximate_period: Traditional 7th century BC, before Nineveh's fall in 612 BC
associated_people: The people of Nineveh / Assyria (subject of his prophecy)
associated_events: Prophesying the fall of Nineveh, capital of Assyria
short_description: A prophet from Elkosh who foretold the violent destruction of Nineveh, capital of the Assyrian empire, as God's judgment for its cruelty.

name: Habakkuk
approximate_period: Traditional late 7th century BC, shortly before the Babylonian invasion
associated_events: Questioning God about the presence of injustice in Judah
Being told God would use the Babylonians to bring judgment
His prayer of trust in chapter 3
short_description: A prophet who openly questioned God about why he would use the wicked Babylonians to judge Judah, ultimately resolving to trust God's justice.

name: Zephaniah
approximate_period: Traditional 7th century BC, during the reign of Josiah
family_members: Father: Cushi (a four-generation genealogy is given in Zephaniah 1:1)
associated_people: King Josiah (his prophecy is dated to Josiah's reign)
associated_events: Prophesying "the Day of the LORD"
Calling for repentance before Josiah's reforms
short_description: A prophet during the reign of King Josiah, Zephaniah warned of the coming "Day of the LORD" and called Judah to seek righteousness before judgment fell.

notes.family_members: Zephaniah 1:1 traces his ancestry back four generations to a "Hezekiah" — some scholars believe this may be King Hezekiah of Judah, though this is debated.

name: Haggai
associated_events: Urging the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple
Prophesying alongside Zechariah
short_description: A post-exilic prophet who urged the returned Jewish exiles to stop delaying and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.

name: Zechariah
associated_events: Receiving a series of eight night visions
Prophesying alongside Haggai to encourage Temple rebuilding
Messianic prophecies later linked to Jesus's life
short_description: A post-exilic prophet who received a series of symbolic night visions and encouraged the rebuilding of the Temple; several of his prophecies are later applied to Jesus in the New Testament.

notes.name: Distinct from the priest Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, in Luke 1.
notes.priest: Nehemiah 12:16 lists a "Zechariah" among priestly family heads of that era, whom many scholars — though not all — identify with this prophet.

name: Malachi
approximate_period: Traditional 5th century BC, likely around or after Nehemiah's time
roles: Last prophet of the Old Testament canon
associated_events: Rebuking Judah's priests for offering blemished sacrifices
Condemning unfaithfulness in marriage
Prophesying a coming messenger to prepare the way (applied to John the Baptist in the NT)
short_description: The final prophet of the Old Testament canon, Malachi rebuked Judah's priests and people for half-hearted worship and looked forward to a coming messenger who would prepare the way of the LORD.

notes.name: "Malachi" (meaning "my messenger") may be a title rather than a proper name, though it is traditionally treated as his name; almost nothing else personal is recorded about him.

name: Jael
associated_events: Offering Sisera shelter and milk in her tent
Killing Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple while he slept
Praised in the Song of Deborah as "most blessed of women"
short_description: Wife of Heber the Kenite, Jael killed the fleeing Canaanite general Sisera by driving a tent peg through his head while he slept in her tent, and is praised in the Song of Deborah.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Celebrated in Judges 5:24 as "most blessed of women," though her method — offering hospitality before killing a sleeping guest — is often discussed as morally complex.

name: Phinehas
associated_events: Stopping a plague by killing an Israelite man and Midianite woman engaged in idolatrous immorality at Baal Peor
Being granted a "covenant of peace" and a perpetual priesthood for his zeal
short_description: Grandson of Aaron, Phinehas stopped a deadly plague at Baal Peor by killing an Israelite and a Midianite woman engaged in idolatrous immorality, earning God's covenant of a perpetual priesthood.

name: Ehud
associated_events: Delivering a hidden double-edged sword to King Eglon of Moab
Assassinating Eglon in his upper chamber
Leading Israel to defeat Moab
short_description: A left-handed judge from the tribe of Benjamin, Ehud assassinated the oppressive Moabite king Eglon with a hidden sword and led Israel to defeat Moab.

name: Onesimus
associated_events: Running away from his master Philemon
Coming to faith through Paul while Paul was imprisoned
Being sent back to Philemon with Paul's letter urging his acceptance as a brother
short_description: A runaway slave who came to faith through Paul in prison, Onesimus was sent back to his master Philemon carrying Paul's letter appealing for his acceptance as a beloved brother rather than a slave.

name: Priscilla
associated_events: Expelled from Rome with other Jews under Emperor Claudius
Hosting a house church with Aquila
Instructing Apollos more accurately in the faith
short_description: A tentmaker and early church leader, Priscilla and her husband Aquila hosted a house church and helped instruct the eloquent preacher Apollos more accurately in the faith.

name: Aquila
associated_events: Expelled from Rome with other Jews under Emperor Claudius
Working alongside Paul as a fellow tentmaker
Hosting a house church with Priscilla
Instructing Apollos more accurately in the faith
short_description: A Jewish tentmaker originally from Pontus, Aquila and his wife Priscilla partnered with Paul in ministry and helped instruct the eloquent preacher Apollos more accurately in the faith.

name: Philip the Evangelist
occupation: One of the seven chosen to oversee food distribution (Acts 6)
associated_events: Chosen as one of the seven to oversee food distribution to widows
Preaching in Samaria with great signs and wonders
Explaining Scripture to and baptizing the Ethiopian eunuch
Later hosting Paul in Caesarea
short_description: One of the seven men chosen to serve the early Jerusalem church, Philip became a traveling evangelist who preached in Samaria and famously explained Scripture to and baptized an Ethiopian court official.

notes.name: Distinct from Philip the Apostle, one of the original Twelve — Acts 21:8 specifically calls him "Philip the evangelist, one of the seven."

name: Jacob
family_members: 12 sons including Joseph, Judah, Reuben, Benjamin
associated_events: Buying Esau's birthright for stew
Deceiving Isaac to receive the blessing meant for Esau
Wrestling with God at Peniel and being renamed Israel
Working 14 years for Laban to marry Rachel and Leah
Reuniting peacefully with Esau
Moving to Egypt in his old age to be with Joseph
short_description: Jacob, grandson of Abraham, deceived his father and brother to obtain the birthright and blessing, then had his name changed to Israel after wrestling with God — becoming father of the twelve tribes.

notes.name: Renamed 'Israel' after wrestling with God at Peniel (Genesis 32:28); both names are used of him throughout Scripture.

name: Isaac
associated_events: Nearly offered as a sacrifice by Abraham on Mount Moriah
Abraham's servant sent to find Rebekah as his wife
Digging wells in Gerar
Blessing Jacob instead of Esau due to Rebekah's deception
short_description: The long-awaited son of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac was nearly offered as a sacrifice on Mount Moriah before God provided a ram instead; he later fathered Esau and Jacob.

name: Joseph
family_members: 10 older half-brothers including Judah and Reuben
associated_events: Given a richly ornamented coat by Jacob
Sold into slavery by his brothers
Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife and imprisoned
Interpreting Pharaoh's dreams and rising to power
Saving Egypt and his family from famine
Forgiving his brothers
short_description: Sold into Egyptian slavery by his jealous brothers, Joseph rose from prisoner to Pharaoh's second-in-command, eventually saving his family from famine and forgiving those who wronged him.

name: Saul
associated_events: Anointed Israel's first king by Samuel
Defeating the Ammonites and Philistines
Disobeying Samuel by offering an unauthorized sacrifice and sparing Amalekite plunder
Growing jealous of David and pursuing him
Consulting a medium at Endor
Dying in battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa
short_description: Anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king, Saul won early military victories but was rejected by God for disobedience, grew consumed by jealousy of David, and died by his own sword after being mortally wounded in battle.

notes.name: This is Saul the first king of Israel — a completely different person from Saul of Tarsus, the persecutor-turned-apostle who took the name Paul (already in this database as 'Paul', alternate name 'Saul of Tarsus').
notes.prophet: Saul twice fell into prophetic ecstasy under the Spirit's influence (1 Samuel 10:10-11; 19:23-24), giving rise to the saying 'Is Saul also among the prophets?' — but he is not counted among Israel's prophets.
notes.violent_death: Wounded by Philistine archers, Saul fell on his own sword to avoid capture (1 Samuel 31:3-4).

name: Goliath
associated_events: Challenging Israel to single combat for 40 days
Defeated by David with a sling and stone
Beheaded by David with his own sword
short_description: A giant Philistine champion over nine feet tall, Goliath taunted the armies of Israel for forty days until the young shepherd David felled him with a single stone from a sling.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Goliath is the story's antagonist, defying 'the armies of the living God' (1 Samuel 17:26) as the enemy champion of the Philistines.

name: Aaron
associated_events: Serving as Moses's spokesman before Pharaoh
Performing signs with his staff
Consecrated as Israel's first High Priest
Making the golden calf while Moses was on Sinai
Dying atop Mount Hor before Israel entered Canaan
short_description: Moses's older brother, Aaron served as Israel's first high priest and spokesman before Pharaoh, though he also crafted the golden calf that led Israel into idolatry at Sinai.

notes.prophet: Aaron is called Moses's 'prophet' in the sense of spokesman (Exodus 7:1), not a prophet in the fuller sense, so this is marked debated.

name: Mary
family_members: Sons: Jesus, James, Joseph, Judas, Simon (Matthew 13:55)
associated_events: The Annunciation
Visiting Elizabeth and singing the Magnificat
Giving birth to Jesus in Bethlehem
Fleeing to Egypt
Present at the wedding at Cana
Standing at the cross
Present with the disciples at Pentecost
short_description: A young woman from Nazareth chosen to be the mother of Jesus after the angel Gabriel announced she would conceive by the Holy Spirit; she later stood at the cross and joined the early disciples in prayer.

notes.name: Distinct from the several other Marys in the Gospels, including Mary Magdalene and Mary of Bethany.
notes.genealogy_recorded: The genealogies in Matthew 1 and Luke 3 are both presented as Joseph's line, though many traditionally read Luke's as tracing Mary's descent; this is debated among scholars.

name: John the Baptist
associated_events: Miraculous birth to elderly parents
Preaching repentance in the wilderness
Baptizing Jesus in the Jordan
Identifying Jesus as the Lamb of God
Imprisoned and beheaded by Herod Antipas at Herodias's request
short_description: Born miraculously to the elderly priest Zechariah and Elizabeth, John preached repentance in the wilderness, baptized Jesus in the Jordan River, and was later beheaded by Herod Antipas.

notes.name: Distinct from John the Apostle (son of Zebedee) and John Mark, both elsewhere in this database.
notes.priest: John was born into a priestly family (his father Zechariah served in the temple), but Scripture presents him functioning as a prophet and baptizer, not as an officiating priest.

name: Judas Iscariot
associated_events: Serving as keeper of the money bag
Objecting to Mary anointing Jesus with expensive perfume
Betraying Jesus for thirty pieces of silver
Identifying Jesus with a kiss in Gethsemane
Death after the betrayal
short_description: One of Jesus's twelve apostles, Judas Iscariot betrayed him to the religious authorities for thirty pieces of silver and died soon after, in anguish over what he had done.

notes.violent_death: Matthew 27:5 records that Judas hanged himself; Acts 1:18 describes him falling headlong so that his body burst open — traditionally harmonized as the rope or branch breaking after he hanged himself, though Scripture does not explicitly state this.

name: Isaiah
associated_events: Vision of the Lord's throne and call to prophesy (Isaiah 6)
Prophesying to King Hezekiah during the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem
Giving Hezekiah a sign by the sun's shadow reversing
Prophecies about a coming Messiah and Suffering Servant
short_description: A major prophet who ministered to Judah's kings across decades, Isaiah is best known for his call vision in the temple and for prophecies about a coming Messiah later quoted throughout the New Testament.

notes.violent_death: Jewish tradition holds Isaiah was martyred under King Manasseh, possibly referenced in Hebrews 11:37, but this is not explicitly narrated in Scripture, so it is marked unknown.

name: John the Apostle
roles: Traditional author of the Gospel of John, three epistles, and Revelation
associated_events: Called from fishing to follow Jesus
Present at the Transfiguration
Reclining next to Jesus at the Last Supper
Entrusted with the care of Jesus's mother at the cross
Outrunning Peter to the empty tomb
Exiled to the island of Patmos where he received the Revelation
short_description: One of Jesus's inner circle of three apostles and traditionally called 'the disciple whom Jesus loved,' John is traditionally credited with writing the Gospel of John, three epistles, and Revelation.

notes.name: Distinct from John the Baptist (a different person entirely, in this database) and from John Mark (author-companion of Paul and Barnabas, also in this database). This is John son of Zebedee, brother of James, one of the Twelve.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditional church history (2nd century onward) attributes the Gospel of John, 1-3 John, and Revelation to this John; modern scholarship debates common authorship of all these works, so this is marked debated.
notes.prophet: As the traditional recipient of the visions recorded in Revelation, John is sometimes regarded as functioning prophetically, though he is primarily identified in Scripture as an apostle.
notes.violent_death: Unlike most of the other apostles, John is traditionally believed to have died of natural causes in old age at Ephesus, though this is extra-biblical tradition rather than Scripture.

name: Thomas
associated_events: Willing to go die with Jesus at Lazarus's tomb (John 11:16)
Asking Jesus how the disciples could know the way at the Last Supper
Doubting the other disciples' report of the resurrection until seeing Jesus's wounds himself
Declaring 'My Lord and my God!'
short_description: Best known as 'doubting Thomas,' this apostle refused to believe Jesus had risen until he could see and touch his wounds himself — after which he declared, 'My Lord and my God!'

notes.violent_death: Early church tradition holds Thomas was martyred while evangelizing in India, but this is not recorded in Scripture, so it is marked unknown.

name: Sarah
associated_events: Renamed from Sarai to Sarah by God
Giving her servant Hagar to Abraham to bear a child
Laughing at God's promise of a son in her old age
Giving birth to Isaac at age 90
Having Hagar and Ishmael sent away
short_description: Abraham's wife and the mother of Isaac, Sarah laughed in disbelief when told she would bear a son at ninety years old, yet is later praised in Hebrews for her faith in God's promise.

name: Rebekah
associated_events: Drawing water for Abraham's servant and his camels at the well
Agreeing to leave home to marry Isaac
Receiving a prophecy that her older son would serve the younger
Helping Jacob deceive Isaac to steal Esau's blessing
short_description: Chosen at a well as a wife for Isaac, Rebekah later favored her son Jacob and orchestrated his deception of Isaac so Jacob would receive the blessing meant for his brother Esau.

name: Rachel
associated_events: Meeting Jacob at the well
Jacob working 14 years for Laban to marry her
Stealing her father's household idols
Long infertility before bearing Joseph
Dying in childbirth with Benjamin
short_description: Jacob's beloved wife and mother of Joseph and Benjamin, Rachel endured years of infertility before finally bearing children, and died giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Bethlehem.

name: Leah
family_members: Sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun
associated_events: Substituted for Rachel on Jacob's wedding night by Laban's trick
Bearing six of Jacob's twelve sons and a daughter
Competing with Rachel for Jacob's affection using mandrakes
short_description: Jacob's first wife, given to him in place of Rachel through her father Laban's deception, Leah bore six sons — including Levi and Judah, ancestors of Israel's priests and kings — and a daughter.

name: Samuel
roles: Prophet who anointed Saul and David
associated_events: Dedicated to the LORD by his mother Hannah before birth
Raised by Eli at Shiloh
Hearing God's call as a boy
Anointing Saul as Israel's first king
Anointing David as king in Saul's place
Confronting Saul over his disobedience
short_description: Dedicated to God before birth by his mother Hannah, Samuel served as Israel's last judge and a great prophet, anointing both Saul and David as king.

notes.priest: Samuel ministered before the LORD at Shiloh and offered sacrifices (1 Samuel 7:9-10), functioning in a priestly role, though Scripture does not identify him as a descendant of Aaron.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Jewish tradition (Talmud, Baba Bathra 14b) credits Samuel with writing Judges, Ruth, and part of 1 Samuel, but this is not stated in Scripture itself.

name: Bathsheba
associated_events: Seen bathing and summoned by David, leading to adultery
Uriah's death arranged by David to cover up the affair
Death of their first child as judgment
Confronted, alongside David, by Nathan's parable
Advocating for Solomon's succession to the throne over Adonijah
short_description: David summoned Bathsheba, then married to Uriah the Hittite, and their adultery led to Uriah's death; she later became David's wife and mother of Solomon, and secured his succession to the throne.

notes.name: Named as 'the wife of Uriah' rather than by her own name in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:6).

name: Delilah
associated_events: Bribed by Philistine rulers to discover the secret of Samson's strength
Repeatedly pressing Samson until he revealed his Nazirite vow
Having Samson's hair cut, leading to his capture
short_description: A Philistine woman bribed by Philistine rulers to discover the secret of Samson's supernatural strength, Delilah wore him down until he revealed it was tied to his uncut Nazirite hair, leading to his capture.

name: Naomi
associated_events: Moving to Moab during a famine and losing her husband and both sons
Urging her daughters-in-law to return to Moab
Returning to Bethlehem with Ruth
Arranging for Ruth to approach Boaz as a kinsman-redeemer
Nursing her grandson Obed
short_description: Widowed in Moab after losing her husband and both sons, Naomi returned to Bethlehem with her loyal daughter-in-law Ruth and helped arrange Ruth's marriage to Boaz, becoming great-grandmother to King David.

notes.name: In her grief, Naomi asked to be called 'Mara' ('bitter') upon returning to Bethlehem (Ruth 1:20).

name: Rahab
roles: Woman of Jericho who hid Israelite spies
associated_events: Hiding Israelite spies sent to scout Jericho
Hanging a scarlet cord from her window as a sign
Spared with her family when Jericho fell
Named in the genealogy of Jesus and praised for her faith
short_description: A Canaanite woman of Jericho, Rahab hid Israelite spies and was spared when the city fell; she is later listed in Jesus's genealogy and praised in the New Testament for her faith.

name: Ezra
roles: Priest and scribe who led a return from exile
family_members: Descendant of Aaron, per the priestly line traced in Ezra 7:1-5
associated_events: Leading a group of exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon
Teaching and enforcing the Law of Moses
Leading public confession over intermarriage with foreign nations
Reading the Law publicly alongside Nehemiah
short_description: A priest and skilled scribe, Ezra led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem, taught and enforced the Law of Moses, and worked alongside Nehemiah to reform the community's religious life.

name: Caiaphas
roles: High priest who presided over Jesus's trial
associated_events: Advising it was expedient for one man to die for the people (John 11:49-52)
Presiding over Jesus's trial before the Sanhedrin
Declaring Jesus guilty of blasphemy
Questioning Peter and John after Pentecost
short_description: The Jewish high priest who presided over Jesus's trial before the Sanhedrin, Caiaphas had earlier counseled that it was better for one man to die for the people than for the nation to perish.

notes.name: Distinct from his father-in-law Annas, the former high priest who also questioned Jesus (John 18:13) and appears alongside Caiaphas in Acts 4:6.

name: Pontius Pilate
roles: Roman official who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion
family_members: Wife: unnamed, who warned him in a dream (Matthew 27:19)
associated_events: Interrogating Jesus and finding no fault in him
Offering to release Jesus or Barabbas to the crowd
Symbolically washing his hands of Jesus's blood
Ordering Jesus's crucifixion
Placing the sign 'King of the Jews' on the cross
short_description: The Roman governor of Judea who, despite finding no fault in Jesus, caved to the crowd's demands and ordered his crucifixion after symbolically washing his hands of the decision.

name: Herod the Great
roles: Roman client king of Judea at Jesus's birth
associated_events: Rebuilding the Jerusalem Temple
Visited by the Magi seeking the newborn 'King of the Jews'
Ordering the massacre of male infants in Bethlehem
Dying shortly after, prompting Joseph and Mary's return from Egypt
short_description: The Roman-appointed king of Judea at the time of Jesus's birth, Herod the Great ordered the massacre of infant boys in Bethlehem after the Magi's visit, in a failed attempt to kill the newborn 'King of the Jews.'

notes.name: Distinct from his son Herod Antipas (who beheaded John the Baptist and questioned Jesus before the crucifixion) and his grandson Herod Agrippa I (who executed James in Acts 12) — both elsewhere in this database's expansion.

name: Vashti
associated_events: Refusing King Ahasuerus's command to display herself before his guests
Deposed as queen for her refusal
Her removal opening the way for Esther to become queen
short_description: The Persian queen who refused King Ahasuerus's command to display her beauty before his guests, resulting in her deposal and setting the stage for Esther to become queen.

name: Elizabeth
associated_events: Barren into old age before conceiving John
Visited by her relative Mary during her pregnancy
The baby leaping in her womb at Mary's greeting
Insisting her son be named John against family expectation
short_description: A descendant of Aaron married to the priest Zechariah, Elizabeth was barren into old age before miraculously conceiving John the Baptist, and welcomed her pregnant relative Mary with a Spirit-filled blessing.

notes.name: Her husband Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, is a different figure from Zechariah the Old Testament prophet also in this database.

name: Zechariah
roles: Priest of the division of Abijah
associated_events: Serving in the temple when the angel Gabriel appeared to him
Struck mute for doubting Gabriel's promise of a son
Regaining his speech upon naming his son John, as instructed
Prophesying the Benedictus over his newborn son
short_description: A priest of the division of Abijah, Zechariah was struck mute after doubting the angel Gabriel's announcement that his elderly wife Elizabeth would bear a son, and regained his speech only after naming the baby John.

notes.name: This is Zechariah the priest, father of John the Baptist — a completely different person from Zechariah the Old Testament prophet already in this database, who lived roughly five centuries earlier during the post-exilic period.
notes.prophet: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Zechariah prophesied the 'Benedictus' (Luke 1:67-79) over his infant son, though he is primarily identified in Scripture as a priest, not a prophet.

name: Jairus
roles: Synagogue official whose daughter Jesus raised from the dead
family_members: Daughter: unnamed, about twelve years old
associated_events: Falling at Jesus's feet to beg healing for his dying daughter
The journey delayed by the healing of a woman with a chronic blood condition
Told his daughter had died
Jesus raising his daughter back to life
short_description: A synagogue ruler who fell at Jesus's feet begging him to heal his dying daughter, Jairus watched Jesus raise her from the dead after she had already died.

name: Tabitha
occupation: Seamstress / maker of clothing for the poor
roles: Disciple in Joppa known for charitable works
associated_events: Known for good works and charity to the poor, especially widows
Becoming sick and dying
Raised from the dead by Peter in Joppa
short_description: A disciple in Joppa beloved for her charity toward widows and the poor, Tabitha (also called Dorcas) died and was raised back to life by Peter, leading many in the town to believe.

notes.name: 'Tabitha' is Aramaic and 'Dorcas' is the Greek translation of the same name (both meaning 'gazelle'); Acts 9:36 gives both.

name: Lydia
roles: Host of a house church in Philippi
associated_events: Heard Paul preach at a place of prayer by a river outside Philippi
Conversion — 'the Lord opened her heart' to respond to Paul's message
Baptism of her household
Hosted Paul and his companions in her home
short_description: A businesswoman from Thyatira dealing in expensive purple cloth, Lydia was the first recorded convert in Europe, coming to faith after hearing Paul preach by a river outside Philippi, then hosting Paul's missionary team in her home.

notes.family_members: Acts 16:15 says her whole household was baptized with her, but no individual family members are named.

name: Simon the Zealot
associated_events: Called and named as one of the Twelve apostles
short_description: One of the Twelve Apostles, known only by his surname 'the Zealot' (or 'Cananaean'), which may point to earlier involvement in a Jewish nationalist movement; Scripture records nothing else about him individually.

notes.name: Distinct from Simon Peter, Simon of Cyrene (who carried Jesus's cross), and Simon Magus (a sorcerer in Acts 8). Called 'the Zealot' in Luke 6:15 and Acts 1:13, and 'the Cananaean' in Matthew 10:4 and Mark 3:18 — likely the same descriptive title, not a reference to the land of Canaan.

name: Simon of Cyrene
roles: Passerby compelled to carry Jesus's cross
associated_events: Compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus's cross to Golgotha
short_description: A man from Cyrene in North Africa who happened to be passing by, Simon was seized by Roman soldiers and forced to carry Jesus's cross on the way to the crucifixion.

notes.disciple: Scripture doesn't say whether Simon was already a follower of Jesus. Mark names his sons Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15:21), suggesting they were known to Mark's original readers, and some connect this Rufus to the one greeted in Romans 16:13 — though that identification isn't certain.
notes.associated_events: John 19:17 states that Jesus carried his own cross, while the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke) all record Simon of Cyrene being compelled to carry it; harmonizations suggest Jesus carried it part of the way before Simon was made to take over.

name: Gamaliel
associated_events: Advised the Sanhedrin to let the apostles go free rather than oppose what might be God's work (Acts 5:34-39)
Taught Paul (Saul) as a young man 'at the feet of Gamaliel' (Acts 22:3)
short_description: A respected Pharisee and teacher of the Law in the Sanhedrin, Gamaliel counseled patience toward the apostles rather than persecution, and was the rabbi under whom a young Saul of Tarsus studied.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Scripture presents him favorably as wise and respected, but doesn't record him becoming a follower of Jesus; later church traditions claiming his conversion are not in the biblical text.

name: Caesar Augustus
approximate_period: Reigned as Roman emperor 27 BC - AD 14
associated_events: Decreed a census of the Roman world (Luke 2:1), which brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem for Jesus's birth
short_description: The Roman emperor who ruled from 27 BC to AD 14, Augustus is mentioned in Scripture only as the ruler whose census decree brought Joseph and Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem, coinciding with Jesus's birth.

notes.king: Augustus held the Roman title of emperor (princeps), not literally 'king' — Rome avoided that title after becoming a republic — but he functioned as the empire's supreme ruler.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
family_members: Son (per Daniel 5, though the exact relation is debated historically): Belshazzar
associated_events: Besieged and destroyed Jerusalem and Solomon's Temple (2 Kings 25)
Took Daniel and other Judean youths captive to Babylon (Daniel 1)
Built a golden image and threw Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego into a furnace for refusing to worship it (Daniel 3)
Struck with madness and living like an animal for a time until he acknowledged God's sovereignty (Daniel 4)
short_description: The powerful king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple and carried Judah into exile, Nebuchadnezzar later suffered a period of madness and, upon his restoration, publicly praised the God of Daniel as the Most High.

notes.family_members: Daniel 5 calls Belshazzar Nebuchadnezzar's 'son' and him Belshazzar's 'father,' though historically Belshazzar was likely a later successor (son of Nabonidus); the Aramaic terms could denote a broader 'predecessor' relationship rather than direct parentage.

name: Balaam
associated_events: Hired by Balak king of Moab to curse Israel but blessed them instead under God's compulsion
His donkey saw the angel of the LORD blocking the path and spoke to him (Numbers 22:28)
Delivered several prophetic oracles blessing Israel, including a prophecy of a 'star out of Jacob' (Numbers 24:17)
Later blamed for counseling Israel's seduction into idolatry and sexual sin at Peor (Numbers 31:16)
Killed by the Israelites during the war against Midian (Numbers 31:8)
short_description: A non-Israelite diviner hired by Moabite king Balak to curse Israel, Balaam instead blessed them under God's compulsion — famously after his own donkey saw an angel and spoke to him — but later became a byword for greed and leading God's people into sin.

notes.prophet: Balaam delivered genuine oracles from the LORD (Numbers 22-24), but he was a pagan diviner by trade and is condemned elsewhere in Scripture (2 Peter 2:15-16, Jude 11, Revelation 2:14) for later counseling Balak to corrupt Israel through idolatry and immorality (Numbers 31:16) — hence the 'mixed' rating.

name: Miriam
roles: Leader of the Israelites during the Exodus
associated_events: Watched over baby Moses in the Nile and arranged for their mother to nurse him (Exodus 2:4-8)
Led the women of Israel in song and dance after crossing the Red Sea (Exodus 15:20-21)
Struck with leprosy for a week after criticizing Moses over his Cushite wife (Numbers 12)
Died and was buried at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1)
short_description: The elder sister of Moses and Aaron, Miriam watched over baby Moses in the Nile, later led Israel's women in celebration after the Red Sea crossing, and was called a prophetess — though she was struck with leprosy for a time after challenging Moses's authority.

name: Cornelius
associated_events: A devout, God-fearing Roman centurion who gave generously and prayed regularly
Visited by an angel instructing him to send for Peter (Acts 10:1-8)
Received the Holy Spirit along with his household while Peter was still speaking (Acts 10:44-48)
Baptized, becoming the first clearly Gentile convert recorded in Acts
short_description: A devout Roman centurion in Caesarea, Cornelius was visited by an angel and directed to send for Peter; his household's reception of the Holy Spirit convinced the early church that the gospel was also for Gentiles.

name: Stephen
roles: One of the seven chosen to oversee food distribution (Acts 6:5)
associated_events: Chosen as one of seven men to oversee food distribution to widows (Acts 6:1-6)
Performed great wonders and signs among the people
Delivered a long speech recounting Israel's history before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7)
Stoned to death while Saul of Tarsus approvingly watched the coats of those stoning him (Acts 7:58-8:1)
short_description: One of the seven men chosen to serve the early Jerusalem church, Stephen was a powerful preacher whose speech before the Sanhedrin so enraged his hearers that he was dragged out and stoned to death, becoming Christianity's first martyr.

name: Silas
associated_events: Sent with Paul and Barnabas to deliver the Jerusalem Council's letter to Antioch (Acts 15:22-32)
Chosen by Paul as a missionary companion for his second journey after the split with Barnabas (Acts 15:40)
Imprisoned and beaten with Paul in Philippi; their midnight praise led to an earthquake and the jailer's conversion (Acts 16:19-34)
Helped write and likely delivered 1 Peter (1 Peter 5:12)
short_description: A leading member of the Jerusalem church and Paul's chosen companion on his second missionary journey, Silas was imprisoned and beaten alongside Paul in Philippi and later helped Peter write his first epistle.

notes.name: Called 'Silvanus' in 2 Corinthians 1:19, 1 Thessalonians 1:1, and 1 Peter 5:12 — the same person as the 'Silas' of Acts.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Traditionally understood as Paul's co-sender/secretary for 1-2 Thessalonians and as the one who physically wrote down 1 Peter at Peter's dictation (1 Peter 5:12), though he isn't considered the primary author of any book.

name: John Mark
roles: Missionary companion of Paul and Barnabas
Traditional author of the Gospel of Mark
associated_events: His mother Mary's house in Jerusalem was a meeting place for the church, where Peter went after his angelic prison escape (Acts 12:12)
Accompanied Paul and Barnabas on the first missionary journey but turned back partway (Acts 13:13)
Caused a sharp disagreement between Paul and Barnabas, who then took Mark with him instead (Acts 15:36-39)
Later reconciled with Paul, who called him 'useful to me for ministry' (2 Timothy 4:11)
Assisted Peter, who calls him 'my son' (1 Peter 5:13)
short_description: A cousin of Barnabas whose early departure from Paul's first missionary journey caused a rift between Paul and Barnabas, John Mark later reconciled with Paul, assisted Peter, and is traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel of Mark.

notes.name: Also called simply 'Mark' or, traditionally, 'Mark the Evangelist' — one person, not a separate figure.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: Early church tradition (e.g., the 2nd-century writer Papias) holds that Mark wrote his Gospel based on Peter's preaching; the Gospel itself does not name its author.

name: Luke
roles: Traditional author of Luke and Acts
associated_events: Called 'the beloved physician' by Paul (Colossians 4:14)
Joined Paul's missionary travels, indicated by the first-person 'we' passages beginning in Acts 16:10
Stayed with Paul during his final imprisonment when others had left (2 Timothy 4:11)
Addressed a two-volume history (traditionally identified as Luke and Acts) to 'most excellent Theophilus' (Luke 1:3, Acts 1:1)
short_description: A physician and Gentile companion of Paul on his missionary journeys, Luke traditionally authored both the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts, and stayed loyally with Paul through his final imprisonment.

notes.wrote_biblical_book: Luke and Acts are internally anonymous but are addressed to the same 'Theophilus' by the same author (Luke 1:3, Acts 1:1); church tradition from the 2nd century identifies that author as Luke the physician. Neither book names Luke directly — his presence is inferred from the 'we' passages in Acts and Paul's letters.

name: James son of Zebedee
approximate_period: Traditional early-to-mid 1st century AD; martyred c. AD 44
roles: Member of Jesus's inner circle (with Peter and John)
associated_events: Called by Jesus along with his brother John while mending fishing nets (Matthew 4:21-22)
Nicknamed by Jesus 'Boanerges,' meaning 'sons of thunder' (Mark 3:17)
Part of Jesus's inner circle present at the Transfiguration and in Gethsemane
He and John (or, per Matthew, their mother on their behalf) asked Jesus for the seats at his right and left in the kingdom (Matthew 20:20-23, Mark 10:35-40)
The first apostle martyred, executed by Herod Agrippa I (Acts 12:2)
short_description: One of the Twelve and part of Jesus's inner circle alongside Peter and John, James son of Zebedee was nicknamed 'Son of Thunder' and became the first apostle to be martyred, executed by Herod Agrippa I.

notes.name: Distinct from James brother of Jesus (leader of the Jerusalem church, not one of the Twelve) and James son of Alphaeus, also called 'James the Less,' another of the Twelve. This James is the brother of John the Apostle.
notes.family_members: Salome is identified as the mother of James and John by comparing Matthew 27:56 with Mark 15:40, which name overlapping groups of women differently; no single verse states this pairing directly.

name: James brother of Jesus
roles: Traditional author of the Epistle of James
associated_events: Along with his brothers, did not believe in Jesus during his earthly ministry (John 7:5)
Jesus appeared specifically to James after the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:7)
Became a leader of the Jerusalem church and presided over the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:13-21)
Called one of the 'pillars' of the Jerusalem church by Paul, alongside Peter and John (Galatians 2:9)
short_description: A younger brother of Jesus who did not believe in him during his earthly ministry, James became a follower after the resurrection and rose to become the leading elder of the Jerusalem church, presiding over the Jerusalem Council.

notes.disciple: James and his brothers did not believe in Jesus during his earthly ministry (John 7:5); he was not one of the original Twelve and became a follower only after a personal resurrection appearance (1 Corinthians 15:7).
notes.apostle: Not one of the Twelve. Galatians 1:19 ('I saw none of the other apostles — only James, the Lord's brother') is ambiguous in the Greek and is sometimes read as loosely calling him an apostle in a broader sense, but he is never listed among the Twelve.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: The Epistle of James identifies its author only as 'James, a servant of God' (James 1:1); tradition attributes it to Jesus's brother rather than James son of Zebedee (martyred early, per Acts 12:2) or James son of Alphaeus.
notes.violent_death: The 1st-century historian Josephus records that James was stoned to death around AD 62 at the order of the high priest Ananus, but this event is not recorded in Scripture itself.

name: Matthew
roles: Traditional author of the Gospel of Matthew
associated_events: Called by Jesus while sitting at his tax booth (Matthew 9:9, called 'Levi' in Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27)
Hosted a large dinner for Jesus attended by 'tax collectors and sinners,' drawing criticism from the Pharisees (Matthew 9:10-11)
short_description: A despised tax collector before Jesus called him, Matthew (also called Levi) left his booth to follow Jesus and hosted a dinner for fellow tax collectors and sinners; he is traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel of Matthew.

notes.name: Called 'Matthew' in Matthew 9:9 and 'Levi' in Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 — one person under two names, common for Jews of the period.
notes.family_members: Mark 2:14 names Matthew's father as Alphaeus — the same name as the father of James son of Alphaeus, another of the Twelve — though Scripture doesn't say whether the two were related.
notes.wrote_biblical_book: The Gospel of Matthew is internally anonymous; the traditional attribution to the apostle Matthew comes from early church writers such as Papias.

name: Andrew
associated_events: Originally a disciple of John the Baptist before following Jesus (John 1:35-40)
Brought his brother Simon Peter to meet Jesus (John 1:40-42)
Pointed out the boy with five loaves and two fish before the feeding of the 5,000 (John 6:8-9)
Brought Greek visitors to Jesus along with Philip (John 12:20-22)
short_description: A fisherman and former disciple of John the Baptist, Andrew was among the first to follow Jesus and immediately brought his brother Simon Peter to meet him; he became one of the Twelve Apostles.

name: Philip the Apostle
associated_events: Called by Jesus in Galilee and immediately found Nathanael (John 1:43-46)
Jesus tested him by asking where to buy bread for the crowd of 5,000 (John 6:5-7)
Approached by Greeks wanting to see Jesus and brought them to him along with Andrew (John 12:20-22)
Asked Jesus to 'show us the Father' at the Last Supper (John 14:8-9)
short_description: One of the Twelve Apostles from Bethsaida, Philip brought his friend Nathanael to Jesus, was tested by Jesus over feeding the 5,000, and famously asked at the Last Supper to be shown the Father.

notes.name: Distinct from Philip the Evangelist, one of the seven chosen in Acts 6 to oversee food distribution, who later preached in Samaria and baptized the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8). This Philip is one of the original Twelve, with a different set of stories, all found in John's Gospel (John 1:43-48, 6:5-7, 12:20-22, 14:8-9).

name: Nimrod
approximate_period: Traditional pre-Abrahamic, shortly after the Flood
associated_events: Described as 'a mighty hunter before the LORD' (Genesis 10:9)
Founded Babel, Erech, Akkad, and other cities in Shinar and Assyria (Genesis 10:10-12)
short_description: A great-grandson of Noah through Ham's line, Nimrod is described as a mighty hunter who became a powerful king, founding Babel and other early cities in Mesopotamia.

notes.good_bad_neutral: Genesis itself doesn't morally condemn Nimrod, but later Jewish and Christian tradition connects him with the founding of Babel and its tower (Genesis 11), which the text does place in the same region shortly after his introduction.

name: Enoch
approximate_period: Traditional pre-flood, per the Genesis 5 genealogy
associated_events: 'Walked with God' for 365 years (Genesis 5:22-23)
Taken by God without dying — 'he was not, for God took him' (Genesis 5:24)
Prophesied about the Lord coming with thousands of his holy ones to execute judgment (Jude 1:14-15)
Commended for his faith, having 'pleased God' before he was taken (Hebrews 11:5)
short_description: Seventh from Adam in the line of Seth, Enoch 'walked with God' and was taken directly into God's presence without dying; he is also remembered for a prophecy about God's coming judgment quoted in the book of Jude.

notes.name: Distinct from an earlier Enoch, son of Cain, after whom Cain named a city (Genesis 4:17) — a different, much less prominent figure.
notes.violent_death: Genesis 5:24 says Enoch simply 'was not, for God took him' — he is one of only two biblical figures (with Elijah) recorded as not experiencing death at all.

name: Methuselah
approximate_period: Traditional pre-flood, per the Genesis 5 genealogy
associated_events: Lived 969 years, the longest lifespan recorded in the Bible (Genesis 5:27)
By the chronology of the Genesis 5 genealogy, his death lines up with the year the Flood began
short_description: The grandfather of Noah, Methuselah lived 969 years — the longest lifespan recorded in the Bible — and, by the chronology of Genesis 5, died around the year the Flood began.

notes.associated_events: Genesis doesn't explicitly say Methuselah died in the Flood itself, only that the ages given in Genesis 5's genealogy place his death around that time; this is a chronological inference, not a directly stated fact.

name: Seth
approximate_period: Traditional pre-flood, per the Genesis 5 genealogy
roles: Third son of Adam and Eve
associated_events: Born to Adam and Eve after Cain killed Abel, 'as a replacement' (Genesis 4:25)
Fathered Enosh, in whose days 'people began to call on the name of the LORD' (Genesis 4:26)
short_description: The third named son of Adam and Eve, born after Cain killed Abel, Seth became the ancestor through whom Genesis traces the godly line leading eventually to Noah.

name: Cain
associated_events: Brought God an offering from his crops that was not accepted, unlike Abel's offering (Genesis 4:3-5)
Murdered his brother Abel out of jealousy and anger (Genesis 4:8)
Cursed by God to be a restless wanderer, marked with a protective sign so no one would kill him (Genesis 4:10-15)
Built the first city, named after his son Enoch (Genesis 4:17)
short_description: The firstborn son of Adam and Eve, Cain became jealous when God accepted his brother Abel's offering but not his own, and murdered Abel — the Bible's first killing — after which God cursed him to a life of restless wandering.

name: Abel
associated_events: Offered God 'the firstborn of his flock,' which God accepted, unlike Cain's offering (Genesis 4:4)
Murdered by his brother Cain out of jealousy (Genesis 4:8)
Called righteous, and commended for his faith; his blood is said to still 'speak' (Genesis 4:10, Hebrews 11:4)
Cited by Jesus as the first in a line of murdered righteous people (Matthew 23:35, Luke 11:50-51)
short_description: The second son of Adam and Eve, Abel was a shepherd whose offering God accepted; his jealous brother Cain murdered him, making Abel the first person to die in Scripture and a byword for righteous suffering.

name: Naaman
roles: Commander of the army of Aram (Syria)
associated_events: A valiant but leprous commander, advised by his wife's Israelite servant girl to seek out the prophet Elisha (2 Kings 5:1-3)
Initially angered when Elisha told him to wash seven times in the Jordan River, expecting something more dramatic (2 Kings 5:10-12)
Healed of leprosy after dipping in the Jordan seven times as instructed (2 Kings 5:14)
Declared 'there is no God in all the world except in Israel' and worshiped the LORD from then on (2 Kings 5:15)
Elisha's servant Gehazi deceitfully took payment from Naaman and was struck with the leprosy Naaman had lost (2 Kings 5:20-27)
short_description: A commander of the Syrian army afflicted with leprosy, Naaman was healed after reluctantly obeying the prophet Elisha's instruction to wash seven times in the Jordan River, and became a worshiper of the God of Israel.

name: Hagar
associated_events: Given to Abraham as a wife by Sarah in order to bear a child (Genesis 16)
Fled Sarah's harsh treatment into the wilderness and was met by the angel of the LORD
Cast out with Ishmael after Isaac's birth (Genesis 21)
God provided water for her and Ishmael in the wilderness after they were sent away
short_description: Sarah's Egyptian servant who became Abraham's wife and bore his firstborn son Ishmael; after Isaac's birth, she and Ishmael were sent away into the wilderness, where God provided for them.

notes.married: Genesis 16:3 describes Sarah giving Hagar to Abraham 'as a wife,' though she continues to be referred to as a servant/maidservant throughout the surrounding narrative.

name: Ishmael
associated_events: Born to Abraham and Hagar (Genesis 16)
Circumcised at age thirteen (Genesis 17:25)
Cast out into the wilderness with Hagar after mocking Isaac at his weaning feast (Genesis 21)
God promised to make him into a great nation
Joined Isaac in burying Abraham (Genesis 25:9)
short_description: Abraham's firstborn son by Hagar, Ishmael was sent away into the wilderness after Isaac's birth but was promised by God to become the father of a great nation; he fathered twelve tribal rulers.

name: Lot
family_members: Sons: Moab and Ben-Ammi (born to him by his daughters)
associated_events: Separated from Abraham and settled near Sodom (Genesis 13)
Captured by invading kings and rescued by Abraham (Genesis 14)
Hosted two angels and shielded them from the men of Sodom (Genesis 19)
Escaped Sodom's destruction; his wife was turned into a pillar of salt for looking back
Fathered Moab and Ben-Ammi through his daughters after fleeing to a cave
short_description: Abraham's nephew who settled near Sodom, Lot was rescued by Abraham from invading kings and later escaped Sodom's destruction with his daughters, though his wife was turned into a pillar of salt for looking back.

notes.good_bad_neutral: 2 Peter 2:7-8 calls Lot 'righteous' and distressed by the wickedness around him, yet Genesis also records troubling episodes, including his offer of his daughters to the mob (19:8) and his later drunkenness and incest with his daughters (19:30-38) — a genuinely mixed portrait.

name: Esau
family_members: Several wives, including Canaanite and Ishmaelite women
associated_events: Born grasping Jacob's heel (Genesis 25:24-26)
Sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew (Genesis 25:29-34)
Lost Isaac's blessing to Jacob through deception (Genesis 27)
Reconciled with Jacob after years apart (Genesis 33)
Became the ancestor of the Edomites
short_description: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin son and a skilled hunter, Esau sold his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of stew and later lost their father's blessing to him as well, becoming the ancestor of the Edomites.

notes.name: Also called Edom (Genesis 25:30, 36:1), the ancestor of the nation of Edom.

name: Judah
roles: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah
Ancestor of the tribe of Judah
Ancestor of King David and, in the New Testament genealogies, of Jesus
family_members: Brothers include Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Joseph, Benjamin
Wife: daughter of Shua, a Canaanite
Sons: Er, Onan, Shelah, and twins Perez and Zerah (by Tamar)
associated_events: Proposed selling Joseph to Ishmaelite traders rather than killing him (Genesis 37:26-27)
Failed to give Tamar his son Shelah as promised, leading Tamar to disguise herself and conceive twins by Judah (Genesis 38)
Offered himself as a substitute slave for Benjamin before Joseph in Egypt (Genesis 44:18-34)
Received Jacob's blessing that the scepter would not depart from his line (Genesis 49:8-12)
short_description: Jacob's fourth son by Leah, Judah proposed selling Joseph into slavery and later fathered twins by his own daughter-in-law Tamar; his tribe became the royal line of David and, in the New Testament genealogies, of Jesus.

notes.name: This is the patriarch, one of Jacob's twelve sons and ancestor of the tribe and later kingdom of Judah — distinct from Judas Iscariot, Judas (Thaddaeus), and Jude the brother of Jesus, all of whom appear elsewhere in this expansion.

name: Barak
roles: Military commander of Israel's army under Deborah
associated_events: Summoned by Deborah to lead 10,000 men against Sisera's army (Judges 4)
Insisted Deborah accompany him into battle
Defeated Sisera's army at the Kishon River
Sisera fled the battle and was killed by Jael rather than Barak, fulfilling Deborah's prophecy
Sang the victory song together with Deborah (Judges 5)
short_description: The military commander whom Deborah summoned to fight Sisera's army, Barak insisted she accompany him into battle; Israel won, but the honor of killing Sisera went to Jael instead of Barak, as Deborah had foretold.

notes.judge: Judges 4-5 identifies Deborah as the judge of that era; Barak is her military commander, though Hebrews 11:32 lists him among Israel's celebrated deliverers of the judges period.

name: Jephthah
associated_events: Driven out by his half-brothers because his mother was a prostitute
Recalled by Gilead's elders to lead them against the Ammonites (Judges 11)
Made a rash vow to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first if granted victory
His daughter came out to meet him, and he carried out his vow
Defeated the Ephraimites and used the word 'Shibboleth' to identify them at the Jordan fords (Judges 12)
short_description: A judge of Israel and the son of a prostitute who was recalled from exile to lead Gilead against the Ammonites, Jephthah made a rash vow before battle that tragically cost him his only child, his daughter.

notes.married: Scripture never states whether Jephthah had a wife, though he is said to have had one daughter (Judges 11:34).

name: Uriah the Hittite
associated_events: While Uriah was away at war, David committed adultery with his wife Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11)
Refused to go home to his wife out of loyalty to his fellow soldiers in the field
David had him placed at the front of the fiercest fighting and ordered the troops to withdraw from him, ensuring his death (2 Samuel 11:14-17)
Named among David's 'mighty men' (2 Samuel 23:39)
short_description: A loyal Hittite soldier in David's army and Bathsheba's husband, Uriah was deliberately placed on the front line of battle and left to die at David's orders after David had committed adultery with his wife.

notes.violent_death: David instructed Joab to put Uriah 'in the front line where the fighting is fiercest' and then withdraw support, engineering his death in battle (2 Samuel 11:14-17).
notes.name: Distinct from Uriah the priest who built an altar for King Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16) and from Uriah son of Shemaiah, a prophet executed by King Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 26:20-23) — this is David's soldier and Bathsheba's husband.

name: Joab
associated_events: Commanded David's army through most of his reign
Killed Abner in revenge for his brother Asahel's death (2 Samuel 3)
Carried out David's order to place Uriah in the front of battle (2 Samuel 11)
Killed Absalom against David's explicit orders to spare him (2 Samuel 18)
Killed Amasa treacherously (2 Samuel 20)
Backed Adonijah's bid for the throne over Solomon and was executed by Benaiah at Solomon's order (1 Kings 2:28-34)
short_description: David's ruthless and loyal nephew, Joab commanded his army for decades, carried out the killing of Uriah the Hittite, killed Absalom against David's orders, and was ultimately executed on Solomon's orders for backing a rival to the throne.

name: Abner
associated_events: Commanded Saul's army (1 Samuel 14:50-51)
After Saul's death, installed Saul's son Ish-bosheth as king and opposed David (2 Samuel 2)
Killed Asahel, Joab's brother, in battle (2 Samuel 2:18-23)
Defected to David's side after a dispute with Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 3)
Murdered by Joab in revenge for Asahel's death (2 Samuel 3:27)
short_description: Saul's cousin and the commander of his army, Abner installed Saul's son Ish-bosheth as king after Saul's death but later defected to David; he was murdered by Joab in revenge for killing Joab's brother Asahel in battle.

name: Michal
family_members: Second husband: Paltiel (Palti) son of Laish, during her separation from David
associated_events: Given to David as a wife after he paid a bride price of Philistine foreskins (1 Samuel 18:20-28)
Helped David escape Saul's assassins by lowering him through a window and disguising an idol as him in the bed (1 Samuel 19:11-17)
Given by Saul to Paltiel while David was a fugitive
Reclaimed by David after he became king (2 Samuel 3:13-16)
Despised David in her heart for dancing before the ark and remained childless the rest of her life (2 Samuel 6:16-23)
short_description: Saul's daughter and David's first wife, Michal helped David escape her father's assassins early on but later despised him for dancing before the ark of the covenant, and Scripture records she remained childless.

name: Zipporah
roles: Daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian
family_members: Father: Jethro (also called Reuel), priest of Midian
associated_events: Met Moses at a well in Midian and became his wife (Exodus 2:15-22)
Circumcised her son and touched Moses's feet with the foreskin at a lodging place, averting God's judgment on Moses (Exodus 4:24-26)
Sent back to Moses by her father Jethro along with their sons after the Exodus began (Exodus 18:1-6)
short_description: The daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian, Zipporah became Moses's wife and, in a strange and difficult episode on the road back to Egypt, circumcised their son to avert God's judgment on Moses.

notes.name: Numbers 12:1 mentions a Cushite wife of Moses; some identify her with Zipporah (a Midianite) and others take her as a different or later wife — the text does not resolve this definitively.

name: Ahab
family_members: Daughter: Athaliah, later queen of Judah
associated_events: Married Jezebel and promoted worship of Baal in Israel (1 Kings 16:29-33)
Repeatedly confronted by the prophet Elijah, including the contest on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18)
Seized Naboth's vineyard after Jezebel arranged Naboth's death (1 Kings 21)
Allied with Jehoshaphat of Judah in wars against Aram
Killed by a stray arrow in battle at Ramoth-gilead, fulfilling a prophecy against him (1 Kings 22:29-40)
short_description: King of Israel and husband of Jezebel, Ahab promoted Baal worship and clashed repeatedly with the prophet Elijah, most notably after seizing Naboth's vineyard; he died from a battle wound at Ramoth-gilead, just as had been foretold.
